title: Harrow Tech - Commitment review & failover playbook
summary: Check-in to review upcoming contract extension figures, discuss capacity uplift for EU region, and agree a failover and fallback playbook for peak traffic. Reviewed security artifacts (SOC2 notes, KMS integration), clarified SSO/SCIM timeline, and agreed on benchmark window for private VPC pilot.
action_items: Maya: send tailored pricing spreadsheet with tiered SLA and burst examples (due 2026-05-21)
Owen: share benchmark checklist and suggested prompt set for latency/cost testing (due 2026-05-20)
Liam: confirm EU data residency constraints and required audit artifacts (due 2026-05-22)
Sofia: schedule 2-hour private VPC window for performance run on 2026-05-28 (due 2026-05-19)
next_steps: Redwood to propose revised commitment tiers and an optional burst add-on
Customer to provision test VPC subnet and share access details for pilot
Schedule follow-up to review pilot results w/ benchmark data (tentative 2026-06-02)
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-18 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Alvarez (Redwood AE), Owen Park (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Harrow Tech - Head of Platform), Sofia Patel (Harrow Tech - SRE Lead), Marcus Li (Harrow Tech - Procurement)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
- Customer considering a 20-35% uplift across US + EU and wants EU private serving for data residency. Concerned about failover when EU capacity peaks. Wants pricing and pilot timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time, uh, really appreciate it. Quick roll call, I’m Maya with Redwood, Owen is our SE, and from Harrow?
[00:08] Liam (Harrow): Liam here, hey.
[00:09] Sofia (Harrow): Sofia, hi.
[00:10] Marcus (Harrow): Marcus on procurement, thanks.
[00:12] Owen (Redwood SE): Hey all.

[00:18] Maya: Cool. Objective for today's sync is to, uh, align on the extension numbers, make sure the EU activation plan fits your residency needs, and walk through a failover playbook — essentially how your app behaves if EU Dedicated is saturated and we need to fallback to hosted or a lower-cost variant.

[00:35] Liam: Yeah that sounds right. Quick context — we've been trending up, our inference units are up about 2.8x q/q for our chat summarization paths. We hit several small spikes last month around european mornings, and that caught some throttles. So main asks: better regional headroom and an operational playbook so our customers don't see 5xxs.

[00:58] Sofia: Also to add, security is non-negotiable — we need KMS/HSM ability (we call it H-M-S in house, sorry), audit logs, and SSO via SAML/SCIM. SOC2 scope is a must for our vendor review.

[01:12] Owen: Totally. On the KMS front Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys — we can walk through the KMS integration doc. Audit logs are surfaced in Console, token-level tracing is available, and we can produce the SOC2 summary artifact. We'll link those after the call.

[01:28] Marcus: From procurement side, pricing matters. We're targeting a 12–18 month extension, want to understand committed capacity tiers and the math on burst. Also curious about any discounts if we commit to EU nodes plus Dedicated reserved capacity in US.

[01:44] Maya: Great, we'll put together a tiered pricing sheet. Preliminary, for the volumes you mentioned a blended committed discount of ~18% is possible if you take a 12 month reserved bundle plus a small burst reserve. We'll quantify in the spreadsheet.

[02:05] Liam: On the technical side, we need to validate end-to-end latency for our longest prompt paths (about 3k tokens) and confirm how KV cache will behave in Dedicated vs Hosted. Any nuances there?

[02:20] Owen: Important question. Dedicated keeps local KV cache per GPU pool — so warm prefixes are very fast and predictable. Hosted can leverage prefix caching as well but there are multi-tenant considerations; latency SLOs differ. Also we have config knobs around continuous batching and target tail latency. For long sequences the kernel selection matters — we can run the same model variant, or a quantized variant if you want lower cost.

[02:46] Sofia: When you say quantized variant, are we talking about 8-bit or some custom 4-bit? We have sensitivity about hallucination increases with lower precision models.

[02:56] Owen: Yeah, we generally recommend 8-bit for production where quality must be preserved; 4-bit can be okay for lower-risk paths. We'll include quality delta guidance from our Optimize tool and suggest prompt-sensitive evals.

[03:12] Liam: Ok that's useful. Another operational question — if EU Dedicated saturates, what's the fallback? We can't send EU customer data to US tenants due to residency.

[03:23] Maya: Right, so the playbook has a couple options depending on your constraints. Option A: hold back requests until capacity frees (queueing) — not ideal for UX. Option B: failover to a compatible EU private node (if you run Private in-region), Option C: degrade model to a smaller in-region variant to preserve residency. Option D: route reads to cached responses where applicable. We can enable granular policy routing per route so sensitive routes never leave EU.

[03:50] Sofia: Degrading the model is appealing if quality delta is small for some of our low-risk endpoints, but for auth or PII redaction flows we need strict residency — must stay in EU.

[04:02] Marcus: Cost play: if we do Dedicated EU + smaller Private footprint, that ups our baseline. What's the recommended combo to get 99.95% availability without huge headroom cost?

[04:15] Owen: A common pattern: reserved Dedicated capacity sized for baseline plus a small Private hot standby for peak failover. Then a burst pool on hosted for non-residency-sensitive workloads. This gives 99.9x availability for EU flows while limiting committed spend. We'll model some scenarios.

[04:39] Maya: We'll run three scenarios for you: conservative (more headroom), balanced (mid headroom + burst), and aggressive-cost-optimized (smaller reserve + more graceful degradation).

[04:49] Liam: Nice. On the security docs, can you send the SOC2 attestations and the KMS integration guide? We need to present to internal audit by May 28.

[04:58] Maya: Yep. I'll attach SOC2 summary, KMS/HSM checklist, and the Console screenshot pack.

[05:05] (minor crosstalk)

[05:12] Owen: For the pilot I want to propose a 3-step benchmark: 1) baseline run on hosted region with your standard prompt set, 2) dedicated EU run with same prompts, 3) failover tests where we simulate saturated Dedicated and observe routing decisions. We recommend 60 minute windows per run.

[05:33] Sofia: 60 minutes per run sounds fine — we can schedule that the week after next. Do you need any agent creds? We'll need to open a temporary VPC peer and share role for logs.

[05:44] Owen: We'll need a service account with read-only metrics access and the ability to spin up a small test job. We'll send an exact checklist.

[05:50] Liam: One more question — what telemetry will you produce during the pilot? We need per-route p50/p95/p99, token-level costs, and per-request trace ids so we can join with our app logs.

[06:03] Owen: Console exports cover p50/p95/p99, token-level cost, and the trace id instrumentation. We'll send a small template for how to ingest trace IDs.

[06:14] Marcus: Procurement question — do you have a standard amendment for adding regions mid-contract? We're likely to add an extra EU region after Q3 and want a clean way to append.

[06:24] Maya: Yes, we have an amendment template for geo additions and capacity top-ups. We can include that in the pricing packet so your legal team can glance.

[06:32] Sofia: Performance nuance — what about cold-start behavior for models with large KV caches when we spin up additional nodes? We saw minutes-long cold windows elsewhere.

[06:42] Owen: Understood. Our runtime supports cache pre-warming via warmup requests and persistent checkpointing for KV caches across pool resizes. Cold-starts should be on the order of seconds if we pre-warm correctly, not minutes. We'll provide the warmup script.

[06:58] Liam: Good. Also want to confirm SSO timeline — we'll need SAML and SCIM for provisioning prior to production cutover.

[07:06] Maya: We can enable SAML and provision via SCIM. Typically that's a 2-week setup from when we have a test IdP and admin contact.

[07:15] Marcus: And any penalty for exceeding committed units during a spike? We prefer automatic burst but want to understand cost.

[07:23] Maya: Bursts are billed at a premium rate; we can also carve out a small buffer that's billed at committed discounted rates to smooth the cost. We'll show both numbers in the spreadsheet so you can choose a policy.

[07:35] Sofia: One edge-case — our compliance team requires that any fallback to hosted must strip customer-identifying metadata even if payload stays in EU. Is that feasible?

[07:44] Owen: Yes, you can configure a pre-send transformation that redacts fields or strips headers on route level. We'll demo examples.

[07:54] (brief pause, typing)

[08:05] Maya: Ok, wrapping toward next steps — we'll deliver the pricing spreadsheet, SOC2/KMS docs, benchmark checklist, and a proposed pilot schedule. On Redwood side Owen will own the benchmark scripts and I will own pricing and contract amendment.

[08:20] Liam: Timeline check — if we get your materials Monday, we can run the VPC prep and aim for the pilot week of May 25th — is that workable?

[08:30] Owen: Week of May 25th works; we have some availability on 25th and 27th for the 60 minute windows.

[08:40] Sofia: I'll book a 2-hour VPC window on the 24th for access prep.

[08:46] Marcus: Procurement will review the amendment; expect us to push back on lead times for invoice cycles, but that's standard.

[08:53] Maya: Understood. Anything else we should capture?

[09:00] Liam: Could you also include a sample failover runbook with play-by-play steps we can give our on-call? Even a one-pager would help.

[09:09] Maya: Absolutely — we'll include a 1-page runbook with the playbook options and recommended thresholds (CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, p99 latency) to trigger each action.

[09:22] (background: keyboard sounds)

[09:28] Owen: Quick note — we mentioned KV cache as K-V cash a few times earlier in our doc, expect a few ASR hiccups in the autogenerated notes.

[09:36] (laughter)

[09:40] Maya: Alright, I'll recap action items and owners in an email after the call. Thanks everyone.

[09:47] Liam: Thanks, bye.
[09:48] Sofia: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notable artifacts referenced (links not included): pricing-spreadsheet-draft.xlsx, soc2-summary.pdf, kms-integration-guide.md, pilot-benchmark-checklist.xlsx, failover-runbook-onepager.pdf
